method: Complete candidate survey followed by individual editorial choices and written reasons, applied to the existing complete guide to keep it within 300 quotations. All verified authorized selections included. Priority given to foundational teachings, substantive explanations, necessary qualifications, distinctive applications, narrative examples and thematic breadth across the sea of bounty in which all things live, emanation from a source that does not become what it sustains, Will and Word in the coming of existence, the unceasing gift, revelation and the renewal of the world, universal bounty and differing receptivity, light within the human reality, kinds of light and spiritual speech, prayer, gratitude and return, becoming a source of help to others, and the supplied philosophical voices. Neither citation count nor source order used as a ranking rule. Imported wording checked separately; version differences remain explicit. The existing reading arc is retained.

selected.text: The Bounty of God is within the heart; it receives the Light
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that the Bounty of God is within the heart, which receives the Light; brief statement of inner reception.

selected.text: The soul is a divine emanation while the body is an earthly composition.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá stating that the soul is a divine emanation while the body is an earthly composition; brings the subject to the human soul and its connected subject.

selected.text: He hath made the world a new world and graced all creation with boundless bounty
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá stating that He has made the world new and graced all creation with boundless bounty; brief statement of renewal.

selected.text: When the heavenly flood flows forth, each valley receives according to its capacity
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá citing that when the heavenly flood flows each valley receives according to its capacity; the Qur’anic image the group’s why names.

selected.text: The ancient bounty is all-encompassing and the favor of the Generous Lord is perfect.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá affirming that the ancient bounty is all-encompassing and the favor of the Generous Lord perfect; concise statement of the subject.

selected.text: When the divine spring is over and the heavenly bounty ceases, the trees of being lie dormant.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that when the divine spring is over and bounty ceases the trees of being lie dormant; the winter image the guide’s questions name.

selected.text: created things have emanated from that True Existence. Thus created things are from Him, not Him.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá answering in Dublin that created things emanated from the True Existence and are from Him, not Him; the shortest formulation of the source-and-creation distinction.

selected.text: From My Most Exalted Pen there hath flowed forth in thy name the Euphrates of mercy and knowledge.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh telling a believer that the Euphrates of mercy and knowledge has flowed from His Pen in his name; personal bounty.

selected.text: Ancient outpourings are like a surging sea and the lights of the All-Merciful like a brilliant star.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá likening ancient outpourings to a surging sea and the lights of the All-Merciful to a star; concise image.

selected.text: Exalted is the Outpourer Who hath caused a pulsing force to flow through the arteries of contingent being.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá praising the Outpourer Who caused a pulsing force to flow through the arteries of contingent being; distinctive image of sustaining life.

selected.text: Again there is the giver of the bounty, the receiver of the bounty and the bounty which is the Holy Spirit.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá naming the giver, the receiver and the bounty which is the Holy Spirit; links the subject to the Holy Spirit.

selected.text: When the light of the Absolute cast a ray upon the world of contingent beings, it illumined the human world.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá stating that when the light of the Absolute cast a ray upon contingent beings it illumined the human world; brief statement of the ray image.

selected.text: The rain-cloud of grace is ever-showering, and the candle of the night-realm of bounty is ever-diffusing its rays
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing the rain-cloud of grace as ever-showering and the candle of bounty ever-diffusing its rays; brief image of ceaseless giving.

selected.text: Know that every mighty matter in the world of existence has a center, and the outpouring emanates from that center.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá teaching that every mighty matter has a center from which the outpouring emanates; principle of a center of emanation.

selected.text: At the dawn of eternity, the Most Great Luminary, the Ancient Beauty, shed its radiance upon the kingdom of the world.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá stating that at the dawn of eternity the Ancient Beauty shed its radiance upon the world; brief statement of revelation as dawn.

selected.text: The breezes of the All-Merciful have wafted from the direction of the Ridvan, and souls have been stirred by their stirring
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh stating that the breezes of the All-Merciful have wafted from the Riḍván and stirred souls; breath of revelation.

selected.text: wherein the Sun of Thy loving-kindness dawned from the horizon of Thy Will and was established upon the throne of Thy mercy
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing the Sun of His loving-kindness dawning from the horizon of His Will; brief image joining Will and mercy.

selected.text: O you who are enchanted by the Face of the Friend! Whatever exists is from Him, and whatever you see is a sign of His bounty.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá stating that whatever exists is from Him and whatever is seen is a sign of His bounty; compact statement of the subject at the opening.

selected.text: And if thou asketh about the infinite bounties of the Abha Kingdom, it is the outpouring of the limitless all-encompassing sea.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing the infinite bounties of the Abhá Kingdom as the outpouring of a limitless sea; concise sea image.

selected.text: Thus have We wafted unto thee a breath from the breezes of the All-Merciful that thou mayest inhale the fragrance of the Most Merciful
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh wafting a breath from the breezes of the All-Merciful that the reader may inhale the fragrance of the Most Merciful; breath as gift.

selected.text: It is clear and evident that there hath never been, nor shall there ever be, any interruption in the outpouring of the All-Bountiful.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh affirming that there has never been nor will be any interruption in the outpouring of the All-Bountiful; direct statement of the arc’s unceasing gift.

selected.text: The infinite favors of God have encompassed all created things, and their manifestations are dependent upon their effort and endeavor.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh stating that God’s infinite favors encompass all things and their manifestation depends on effort and endeavor; the guide’s key text on effort.

selected.text: Infinite bounties have encompassed all, and successive effulgences have unveiled themselves. The lights have illumined both East and West
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá stating that infinite bounties have encompassed all and successive effulgences have illumined East and West; succession of divine outpourings.

selected.text: through whom the ocean of Thy knowledge surged amidst Thy creation and the fragrance of Thy loving-kindness wafted throughout Thy dominion
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing one through whom the ocean of His knowledge surged and the fragrance of His loving-kindness wafted; bounty through a chosen soul.

selected.text: Although the essences of created things exist through the reflection of His light, alas they are unaware of Him and without fruit or trace
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá lamenting that things exist through His light yet remain unaware of Him; dependence unrecognized, echoing the opening fish image.

selected.text: All the saplings of the world have appeared from one Tree, and all the drops from one Ocean, and all beings owe their existence to one Being.
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá stating that divine guidance and spiritual outpourings are sheer gift and absolute grant; keeps grace from being something earned.

selected.text: Today all created things are growing and moving through the outpourings of the Most Great Name, and are drawing sustenance and being stirred.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá stating that all things now grow and move through the outpourings of the Most Great Name; sustaining bounty in this Day.

selected.text: His aid and grace can transform a weak bird into an eagle of the Supreme Concourse and an insignificant atom into a star of the ethereal sphere.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá stating that His grace can transform a weak bird into an eagle and an atom into a star; concise image of transformation.

selected.text: Today the true Beneficent One is manifest, and the sea of bounty is surging, and the effulgences of the Sun of generosity are visible and evident
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh announcing that the true Beneficent One is manifest and the sea of bounty is surging today; links bounty to the present revelation.

selected.text: and the breezes of grace have wafted from the source of bounty, and rock and clod and tree have been blessed by the favors of the Lord of destiny
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing breezes of grace blessing rock, clod and tree; bounty reaching even the humblest things.

selected.text: The loving-kindness and grace of the Divine Unity, and His bounty and tender mercy, encompass and pervade the entire created world like unto rain.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá stating that God’s grace and tender mercy encompass and pervade the entire created world like rain; direct statement of all-pervading bounty.

selected.text: The divine bounties are likened to water. He says We send down water from heaven. Rivers and streams flow according to their measure and capacity
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that divine bounties are likened to water, rivers flowing according to their measure and capacity; water and capacity.

selected.text: Who through the attraction of the Most Exalted Word brought being out of utter nothingness, and from non-existence made manifest the signs of eternity
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh praising Him Who through the attraction of the Most Exalted Word brought being from utter nothingness; the Word as origin of existence.

selected.text: Say: By God! This is a Day whereon the breezes of the All-Merciful have wafted, and the fragrance of musk hath been diffused from this glorious station.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh proclaiming a Day in which the breezes of the All-Merciful have wafted; breath image in this Day.

selected.text: The Ancient Beauty hath made the world of humanity the envy of the realm of dominion through the effulgent light of His revelation and manifest bounty.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá stating that the Ancient Beauty has made humanity the envy of the realm of dominion through His revelation and bounty; revelation’s effect on the human world.

selected.text: The rain of mercy bestows life upon all created things, even unto the pearls within the seashells of the sea which are connected to this boundless grace.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá stating that the rain of mercy gives life to all things, even the pearls within seashells; image of bounty reaching every hidden place.

selected.text: All this is from the mines of Thy bounty, the treasuries of Thy grace, the wonders of Thy favor, the keys of Thy mercy, and the springs of Thy generosity.
selected.reason: The Báb’s prayer acknowledging all as from the mines of His bounty and springs of His generosity; gratitude in the Báb’s voice.

selected.text: through Thy Name the All-Giving, take up a chalice of the water of life and, through Thy Name the All-Bountiful, pass it round among all contingent beings
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh asking that a chalice of the water of life be passed among all contingent beings through the Name the All-Bountiful; prayer for universal bounty.

selected.text: Thus did the earth of realities quiver and swell with the waters of revelation descending from the heaven of the Revealer, bringing forth every goodly kind.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing the earth of realities quivering and swelling with the waters of revelation; Qur’anic image of revival.

selected.text: The ocean of grandeur hath been stirred by the winds that blow from the source of the supreme bounty, casting the pearls of bestowal upon the shores of hope.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing the ocean of grandeur stirred by winds from the source of supreme bounty casting pearls on the shores of hope; complete form of the image.

selected.text: The doors of My favors, which from the beginning that hath no beginning until now had remained sealed, are now opened in truth by the finger of ancient glory.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh declaring that the doors of His favors, sealed from the beginning, are now opened by the finger of ancient glory; marks the new outpouring.

selected.text: This is certainly so, for the sustenance of existence comes from the All-Bountiful. If sustenance from God did not reach existence, no created thing would move.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá stating that the sustenance of existence comes from the All-Bountiful and without it no created thing would move; restores the guide’s question about motion.

selected.text: Today the Kawthar of knowledge floweth from the Pen of the All-Merciful, and the Euphrates of mercy descendeth as rain from the heaven of the chosen One's grace.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh declaring that the Kawthar of knowledge flows from the Pen and the Euphrates of mercy descends as rain; flowing-water image of revelation.

selected.text: However, when the confirmations of the All-Merciful and the assistance of the Eternal shine forth in human reality, this becomes a source of glory and brings joy.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá stating that when divine confirmations shine in human reality they become a source of glory and joy; light within the human reality.

selected.text: Every created thing hath had and still hath a fragrance peculiar unto itself, and that fragrance is, in one sense, a messenger, inasmuch as it guideth men unto it.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh stating that every created thing has its own fragrance which is in one sense a messenger guiding to it; distinctive image of speech in creation.

selected.text: God created from the Will an essence of volition with perfect potentiality therein. Then God created from that essence the five gardens and their seven precincts
selected.reason: The Báb stating that God created from the Will an essence of volition and from it the gardens; brief statement of the Will as first created.

selected.text: The Most Great Unity hath manifested Its all-merciful effulgence, and hath made contingent existence a mirror reflecting the images of the realm beyond contingency.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá stating that the Most Great Unity has made contingent existence a mirror reflecting the realm beyond contingency; mirror image of creation.

selected.text: The seas moved"—the seas of existence; the seas of life; the seas of sciences; the seas of knowledge; the seas of understanding; the Seas of the Love of GOD rolled
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá interpreting “the seas moved” as seas of existence, life, knowledge and love; spiritual reading of an image.

selected.text: Thus the purpose of the world of creation is the realization of things through the bounty of existence, and this is among the requirements of divine grace and bounty
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá stating that the purpose of the world of creation is the realization of things through the bounty of existence, required by divine grace; gives existence itself as gift.

selected.text: Through the movement of the Will, resplendent waves arose, and these waves in one station are His manifestations of Names and attributes that have encompassed the world.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing resplendent waves arising from the movement of the Will as His manifestations of Names and attributes; distinctive image of the Will in motion.

selected.text: Likewise the divine qualities that were manifested from that Dawning-Place of heavenly bounties - those qualities too are the heavenly sustenance of the Incomparable Lord.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá stating that the divine qualities manifested from the Dawning-Place of bounties are the heavenly sustenance of the Lord; spiritual sustenance.

selected.text: As for the passage in the Iqan, it explains that those holy souls continuously receive outpourings and assistance from the Reality of Divinity and the All-Glorious Essence.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá explaining a passage of the Íqán that holy souls continually receive outpourings from the Reality of Divinity; continuous reception by the Manifestations.

selected.text: It is the True Cup-bearer Who, from time immemorial and unto all eternity, hath bestowed and continues to bestow the choice wine of inner meanings upon the world of humanity.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing the True Cup-bearer Who from eternity bestows the wine of inner meanings on humanity; continuity of spiritual bounty.

selected.text: These are trees planted in the garden of Thy love, growing on the banks of the rivers of Thy bounty, verdant and fresh through the outpourings of the clouds of Thy guidance.
selected.reason: Prayer of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá for souls as trees growing on the banks of the rivers of His bounty; prayerful image of growth.

selected.text: We have brought forth for thee from the ocean of inner meanings the pearl of remembrance and utterance, that thou mayest give thanks unto thy Lord, the Lord of all religions.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bringing forth the pearl of remembrance from the ocean of inner meanings so the believer may give thanks; gratitude as response.

selected.text: The outpourings are descending like torrential rain, and the manifestations of the Abha Beauty are succeeding and following one after another from the Dayspring of the Unseen.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing outpourings like torrential rain and successive manifestations from the Dayspring of the Unseen; succession of bounty.

selected.text: The Most Great Sea hath turned toward you, desiring to adorn the heart of your heart and the sight of your sight with My wisdom and utterance which lay hidden within its shells.

selected.text: Since the day when the Ancient Ocean began its Most Great outpouring and ceaseless surging, the waves of divine bounties have stormed the shores of existence from every direction
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing the Ancient Ocean’s ceaseless surging and waves of bounty storming the shores of existence; continuity of revelation.

selected.text: When God created the Point, He caused it to descend to the worlds of existence openly and called it to approach by command. It answered the All-Merciful in humility and submission.
selected.reason: The Báb describing God causing the created Point to descend to the worlds and the Point answering in submission; image of the first creation’s response.

selected.text: And the Hidden and Treasured One, Who was forever concealed in the divine treasury of infallibility, has in these days been made manifest - a bounty from His presence upon the world.

selected.text: By God, the ocean of grace has surged, and the fragrance of justice has wafted, and the sun of bounty has shone forth, and the clouds of generosity rain upon all who are in existence.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh swearing that the ocean of grace has surged and the clouds of generosity rain upon all in existence; universal outpouring in this Day.

selected.reason: Prayer of Bahá’u’lláh asking not to be denied the breezes of Revelation and the fragrant emanations of the robe of mercy; petition to receive.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing the breeze of the All-Merciful, the radiant morn and the call to awakening from the Abhá Kingdom; brings breath and light into the revelation arc.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá stating that bounties descend like torrential rain and all atoms receive a portion of the names and attributes; universality of reception.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá stating that the outpouring of the Holy Spirit turns an acorn into a tree and black soil into a rose garden; image of spiritual growth.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá likening the breeze of holiness to a spring breeze and April rain bestowing new life; spring imagery for spiritual renewal.

selected.text: He sendeth down upon whomsoever He willeth among His creatures that which draweth him to the holy court, the dawning-place of a mighty Name. Say: His favor hath encompassed all created things
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh stating that His favor has encompassed all created things while He draws whom He wills to His court; joins universal favor and particular guidance.

selected.text: The clouds of bounty are overflowing, and the outpouring of witnessed grace giveth life to both worlds. The sea of favors is surging with waves, and the waves of benevolence rise ever higher.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing overflowing clouds of bounty giving life to both worlds and the surging sea of favors; joins rain and sea images.

selected.text: Human reality is a divine trust, and the human world represents its natural emanations. That divine trust is a brilliant light, while these natural emanations are the darkness of the furnace.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá distinguishing human reality as a divine trust of light from the natural emanations that are the furnace’s darkness; necessary distinction within the human being.

selected.text: He hath caused us to reach the summit of heaven from the darksome pit in which we were. He hath enabled us to attain the apex of the realm of the Concourse from the nadir of our degradation.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá giving thanks that He raised us from the darksome pit to the summit of heaven; gratitude for transforming bounty.

selected.text: all that is infinite hath been created by One Who is infinite. Limitations are a characteristic of the finite, and restriction is a quality of existent things, not of the reality of existence
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá in the Tablet of the Celestial Spheres stating that limitation belongs to existent things, not to the reality of existence; necessary metaphysical qualification.

selected.text: Though the outpouring of spring rain may adorn meadow and plain and make mountain and valley verdant, the heavenly outpouring and the rain of divine mercy adorns the life-giving expanse of heart and soul
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá contrasting spring rain that adorns meadows with divine mercy that adorns heart and soul; distinguishes physical from spiritual bounty.

selected.text: The portals of His abundant grace have opened wide through the sustaining breaths of the Holy Spirit. The fragrant breezes of His life-giving bounty bringeth solace to the heart and comfort to the yearning.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing the portals of grace opened through the breaths of the Holy Spirit and life-giving breezes bringing solace; breath and the heart.

selected.text: The infinite outpourings of divine grace have encompassed the world of existence and the realm of being, and the lights of sanctification of the Glorious Lord have illumined the horizons of contingent beings.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing the infinite outpourings of divine grace encompassing the world of existence; clear statement of all-encompassing grace.

selected.text: In these days when the lights of the Abha Kingdom have encompassed the worlds of existence, and the waves of the Most Great Sea have filled the shores of contingent beings with the pearls of divine outpourings
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing the waves of the Most Great Sea filling the shores of contingent beings with pearls of divine outpourings; sea image of revelation.

selected.text: The dawning-places of creation are illumined by the lights of their beauty, and both the East and West of contingent being have become a rose-garden and flower-field through the outpourings of their perfection.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing the dawning-places of creation illumined and East and West made a rose garden through the outpourings of perfection; renewal image.

selected.text: Shedding its effulgent rays upon the East and the West, the North and the South, and all the horizons and regions of the world, it hath, through its bounteous grace, nurtured the realities of all created things

selected.text: these kindnesses are from the overflowing characteristics of the Lord of Clear Proofs upon the subtle realities of beings, which have received and continue to receive emanations from the all-encompassing Reality

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá likening God’s favors to a boundless ocean and winter clouds that refresh the hearts of the attracted; ocean and rain joined to the heart.

selected.text: by the wafting of the breezes of Thy grace whereby Thou didst quicken all created things and caused them to speak forth Thy praise, and didst bring forth all beings and shed upon them the lights of Thy countenance

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing God’s grace as a boundless ocean submerging all things and casting pearls on the hearts of the faithful; ocean image of universal grace.
